headline: Trump: deportations were 'too tough'. His team: no change.
summary: Trump told CBS's 60 Minutes Sunday that his deportation policy 'might have been too tough' and both helped and hurt his party in the midterms. The same day the White House said it will not slow down, and Homeland Security said ICE is 'NOT backing away'. Exit polls put immigration third for voters, after the economy and democracy.

cover_question.q: If it was too tough, does it stop?

cover_answer: No. The White House says ICE isn't slowing down.
table_question: If you admit you went too far, do you have to change?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: The president has been sending people who came to the US without permission back to where they came from. Sunday he said on TV that maybe he was too tough about it, and that it cost his side votes. His helpers said nothing will change. Like a coach who says practice was too hard, then runs it again. The grown-ups are arguing it out.
5-7.why: The coach carries it. At seven one picture stands for the whole event.
5-7.why_long: A seven-year-old takes one vivid feature for the whole event, so the script gives them a coach who calls practice too hard and then runs it again, and keeps the arrests and the protests out. Expect "are they sending my friend away?" Say what you know about your own town, and that the policy has not changed.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: Trump's government has been deporting people who are in the US illegally, and ICE was told to aim for 2,700 arrests a day. On Sunday Trump said the policy 'might have been too tough'. His White House said the same day it won't slow down. A referee who admits a harsh call, then keeps calling it.
8-12.why: Policy, election, admission, no change: a chain they follow at 11.
8-12.why_long: At 11 they are testing whether adults apply their own rules, so the script runs the chain: a policy, an election lost, a president who says too tough, a White House that says carry on. The referee is the mechanism. Expect "so which one is true?" Both were said the same day. Watch what ICE does.

13-17.script: If a president says his policy 'might have been too tough', then what? Trump said it Sunday, about deportations. That day his spokeswoman said none has been stronger on enforcement, and ICE's target is 2,700 arrests a day. Second: which is policy, the interview or the statement?
13-17.why: Interview and statement, both on the record. At 14 they can hold both.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things at once, so the script sets the interview against the statement, both from the same day, and asks which one is the policy. Expect "so he admitted he was wrong?" Not quite. He said it both helped and hurt. Vance went further: open to focusing on businesses that hire illegal labour.

5-7.a: Sending someone back to the country they came from.

8-12.q: Why did he say it was too tough?
8-12.a: He thinks it cost his party votes. Polls put immigration third for voters.
The White House says no. ICE says it's not backing away or slowing down.

13-17.q: If it was too tough, does it stop?
13-17.a: No. The White House and Homeland Security say nothing slows down.

13-17.q: What did Vance want to change?
13-17.a: He wrote he's open to focusing on businesses that hire illegal labour.
